title: Envelope
description: The single message shape for the whole system.

admin.description: Set when the sender holds `admin = true` in the spec.

op_id.description:
Idempotency key: mandatory for Task, Completion, Control.

`None` is legal only for [`MsgKind::Note`], and [`Envelope::validate`] enforces that: a Task, Completion, or Control without a key is refused on the field `op_id`, so the retry the sender eventually makes dedups on one id.

A note that needs a durable row — the client queues every outbound envelope keyed by its `op_id` — is stamped once by the code that writes the row, and the stamped envelope is what gets stored and replayed (see `stamp_op_id` in `onlyne-client`). So the absent key here never means "mint one per attempt": a caller that generated a fresh id on every read would key each retry as a new send, and idempotence would silently stop existing. Keep `op_id` as received, and stamp before the first write.

ttl_ms.description: Notes expire; a queued note past its deadline is settled `expired`.

Body.description: Envelope payload: text plus at most one inline image.

head.description: One display line the sender names for this body, which a reader shows in place of a preview of the body's own text. `None` is the ordinary case: the body's text is the only content, and a store that keeps a one-line preview derives it from the text. A completion that carries its full result in `text` and a one-line summary separately sets this, so the summary is what a ledger shows rather than the first clusters of the result.

Causality.description: Causality chain over one task family.

deadline.description: Wall-clock bound for the whole family.

family.description: The family's root task id. Every task handed on from one root carries the same family, which is what lets a supervisor read a whole run as one arc instead of walking `parent_task` links, and what `onlyne ledger` prints beside the hop. A root minted before this field existed names none, and the first child mints the family from its own parent.

hop.description: Hop count from the root task.

hop_budget.description: The hops this family may spend, set by whoever started it. A role reads it to learn whether it is the hop that keeps the task, which keeps that budget out of the task text.

labels.description: Free-form metadata the core carries and never interprets. Bounded by [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_MAX_ENTRIES`], [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_KEY_MAX_BYTES`], and [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_VALUE_MAX_BYTES`] at [`Envelope::validate`].

origin.description: The role this family reports home to, when the sender is not that role.

parent_task.description: The task that caused this one, when downstream.

task.description: Task family id, uuid v4, minted when the work is created.

ControlOp.description: A command over an existing task.

oneOf.description: Tear the session down and release its slot.
Ask the owning client for a fresh probe of the resource.
Ask for the full lifecycle projection right now.
Abandon the task and settle it as cancelled.
Bring the task's live session to the front of its host.

ImagePart.description: One inline image, carried base64 inside the envelope.

MsgKind.description: Delivery intent and queueing class (decision D11, D10).

oneOf.description: Hand work to a role, creating or reusing a session.
Free text. Never queued, never creates a session.
Lifecycle command over a task: recycle, probe, snapshot, cancel.

Principal.description: Process-local identity of a message sender.

oneOf.description: A role in the cluster, optionally narrowed to one of its sessions.
An external IM conversation reached through a gateway.
A subordinate cluster, used by admin and aggregate reporting only.
